L2835@P67: Measurement and correction of atmospheric effects in O2-B and O2-A absorption bands in
L2836@P67: the context of sun-induced fluorescence remote sensing
L2837@P67: F. Daumard, Y. Goulas and A. Ounis, Laboratoire de Météorologie Dynamique, Ecole Polytechnique, France
L2838@P67: R. Pedros, Universitat de Valencia, Departament de Fisica de la Terra i Termodinamica, Valencia, Spain
L2839@P67: I. Moya, Laboratoire de Météorologie Dynamique, Ecole Polytechnique, France
L2840@P67: Abstract : Under sun-light illumination, the shape of the atmospheric oxygen bands (O2-B, 687 nm and O2-A, 760 nm)
L2841@P67: of the vegetation radiance is modified by chlorophyll fluorescence. However for far- range measurements, atmospheric effects also
L2842@P67: modify this shape. In this study, measurements in O2-A and O2-B absorption bands have been performed at different altitudes up
L2843@P67: to 3123 m over bare soil and wheat fields. It is observed that bands depth increase significantly with altitude. In O2-B band, the
L2844@P67: total magnitude of variation is of the same order of magnitude as the change induced by vegetation fluorescence, while it is much
L2845@P67: greater in O2-A band. We used MODTRAN 4 to correct measurements from these atmospheric effects and to retrieve ground
L2846@P67: level band depths. It is found that the variation of corrected band depth with altitude is greatly reduced. These results show that
L2847@P67: MODTRAN 4 can be used to account for atmospheric effects. We also showed that an accurate evaluation of the contribution of
L2848@P67: environment is needed to correct band depth from atmospheric effects, especially in the O2-B band.
L2849@P67: A FLUORESCENCE RETRIEVAL METHOD FOR THE FLEX SENTINEL-3 TANDEM MISSION
L2850@P67: N. Sabater, L. Alonso and J. Vicent, Image Processing Laboratoy (IPL), University of Valencia
L2851@P67: S. Cogliati, Remote Sensing of Environmental Dynamics Laboratory, University of Milano-Bicocca, Italy
L2852@P67: J. Verrelst and J. Moreno, Image Processing Laboratoy (IPL), University of Valencia
L2853@P67: Abstract : A new fluorescence retrieval method is proposed to support ESA’s 8th Earth Explorer Fluorescence EXplorer
L2854@P67: (FLEX) candidate mission. Most hyperspectral fluorescence retrieval algorithms available in the literature are very sensitive to
L2855@P67: true reflectance modelization and/or they assume the atmospheric status as known. The proposed algorithm delivers the retrieval
L2856@P67: of full fluorescence spectrum at canopy level by using only Top Of Atmosphere (TOA) radiances as input. The proposed method
L2857@P67: starts with the atmospheric correction of TOA radiances, characterizing the state of the atmosphere without assuming any a-priori
L2858@P67: classification on aerosols models, performing a first estimation of fluorescence values in main oxygen absorption bands without
L2859@P67: any approximation of true reflectance spectrum, and using this fluorescence estimation to initialize a Spectral Fitting Method
L2860@P67: (SFM) to finally retrieve a full fluorescence spectrum. All these aspects make the proposed fluorescence retrieval method robust
L2861@P67: and independent of external auxiliary data.

L2880@P67: Abstract : In this contribution we present activities and selected results obtained in recent studies and campaigns conducted in the context of the FLuorescence EXplorer (FLEX) mission. FLEX is a candidate mission for the ESA 8th Earth Explorer
L2881@P67: and large efforts are currently dedicated to the development of an implementation scheme for an accurate mapping of fluorescence
L2882@P67: from the selected spaceborne sensor and mission configuration. Field and airborne data collected in different experimental campaigns, together with simulated data, have been used to demonstrate the feasibility of fluorescence retrievals and the potential of
L2883@P67: exploiting high spatial resolution fluorescence maps for a better understanding of the environment from space.
